newsitem.title: USA: Western U.S. spot power drops as demand eases.
newsitem.headline: Western U.S. spot power drops as demand eases.

text.p: Spot power prices in the western U.S. fell slightly Thursday amid expectations of slower autumn demand.

When the Bonneville Power Administration withdrew its offer for heavy-load power on Wednesday, "everyone kind of went into a panic," explained one trade source. "But there is plenty of power out there and not that much demand."
He noted that temperatures in the desert Southwest are still high, but weather along the coast and in California--which accounts for the bulk of regional load demand--has cooled off.
"I think some people got caught long at COB," said a trader at a California utility. "The weather has been mild up there."

Next-day firm prices at the California-Oregon border (COB) were last seen at $17.00-18.00 per megawatt hour, down from 18.50-19.00 on Wednesday. Palo Verde was quoted $25.00-26.00, compared with close to $27.00 on Wednesday.
Quotes for next-day power at Four Corners were also seen down at $21.00, compared with $24.00 early this week.
COB prices for October, however, were reported creeping up to $16.50-16.65, compared with $15.70-16.20 on Wednesday.
"I think it's just a short-term bump, there is plenty of room for prices to come down," said another trader.
Palo Verde for October was down slightly today at $16.50-16.65, compared with $16.55-16.80 on Wednesday.
